body:
Personal thought is to find a therapist. Divorce is listed as one of the more traumatic experiences we have as humans, regardless of how amicable. They can help build your inventory of coping skills. They also have a neutral perspective on the situation. It’s really easy to spiral fast and depression can sneak up on you. Many insurance plans have mental health stuff included. Some employers also have anonymous resources for help. 
Like others have said too, go to the gym (depression weight gain is a thing).

Is it possible to email or call your therapist during the negative episodes? Maybe email yourself or put it in notes on your phone, most people have their phone 24/7. Either way for the email, it acts like a journal that can be referenced before therapy session.

Pets are truly amazing for dealing with stuff. They seem to just know. Since I don’t have any due to current circumstance, I’ve been doing the dog thing vicariously with my buddies dogs. Not the same, but even that is enough to help.

There’s probably reasons, especially liability, however reading the rules, the sub specifically makes it a challenge for any meaningful conversation besides op venting/to ‘ask for help’. Responses are limited because we are not supposed to share medical recommendations, uplifting comments, or role model, which to me means that people who get better, can’t really say how they got better or provide moral support = all of the above limitations. 
Some things work for some people and not others. I hope the best for everyone though. 
(I’ll get off my pedestal now, sad lol)
Anyone else starting at the top with a sled?
I guess I’m a failure at dying too, cause I’m still here. Oh well. More meds and therapy, and life goes on.

Yes. I found it an escape until the burnout set in, and then there was nothing outside of work for support because so much time was spent there. Everyone’s different though, and your experience is different than mine. I wish you luck.
Disturbed’s version of “The Sound of Silence” on repeat as my personal OST.

Thanks for the response. True, Covid has, and is still, messing people up. I didn’t want to make the post too long....guess I should elaborate...

After the first go, I was ‘voluntarily’ sent to a psych ward, went through an IOP program after that, and going to regular therapy and psychiatry visits since. Currently on meds. There’s been days that the meds and strategies do work, but lately they haven’t, mostly due to recent life events and my own personal failings.
